topics.title: Communication Culture
topics.scope: Clear messages, confirmation, understandable instructions and learning from near misses.

topics.title: Cyber Wellness
topics.scope: Personal cyber hygiene and awareness of shipboard digital risks.

questions.question: A new crew member cannot understand the language used in an SMS instruction. What should the company arrange?
options: A signature confirming receipt only
Relevant information in a working language the crew member understands
Informal guessing from the equipment labels
A copy with more technical abbreviations
questions.explanation: Receiving a document is not the same as understanding it. The SMS information must be understandable to the personnel who use it.

questions.question: Which instruction style best supports the master’s safety responsibilities?
options: A clear, simple instruction
A long message with several unexplained abbreviations
A hint that requires the listener to infer the task
An instruction left incomplete to save time
questions.explanation: Clear, simple instructions reduce avoidable ambiguity. This principle supports effective communication about safety duties.

questions.question: During a VHF exchange, noise hides part of a message. Which response addresses that problem?
options: Acknowledge the part you guessed
End the exchange without explanation
Ask the sender to say the message again
Treat silence as agreement
questions.explanation: A message that was not properly received needs repetition. Guessing can change its meaning.

questions.question: You hear every word of a VHF message but cannot understand its meaning. What should you communicate?
options: The message has been completed
The message is not understood
Your radio is switched off
You accept the instruction
questions.explanation: Hearing and understanding are different. State the lack of understanding so clarification can follow.

questions.question: A VHF message contains advice. Which reply gives the sender the clearest check of what you understood?
options: A brief sound without words
Only the sender’s name
No reply until the next watch
A reply repeating the substance of the advice
questions.explanation: Repeating the substance lets the sender detect a misunderstanding. A vague acknowledgement does not show what advice was received.

questions.question: While transmitting an SMCP message, you notice that you gave an incorrect value. What is the appropriate communication approach?
options: Mark the mistake and give the corrected information
Continue and hope the listener notices
Repeat the original incorrect value louder
Replace the subject without indicating a correction
questions.explanation: An explicit correction distinguishes the intended information from the earlier error. The SMCP provides a correction convention for this purpose.

questions.question: You are asked for information that is not yet available but will be available shortly. Which SMCP approach fits?
options: Supply an estimate as a confirmed fact
Remain silent without explanation
Indicate stand-by and give the expected time interval
Announce a distress signal
questions.explanation: A stand-by response with a time interval communicates the delay without inventing information.

questions.question: Two safety-related SMS tasks appear to have no assigned person. What management arrangement is needed?
options: Leave responsibility to whoever happens to be nearby
Define responsibilities and communicate the assignments
Assume the newest crew member is responsible
Wait for a near miss to settle ownership
questions.explanation: Documented responsibilities make it clear who manages, performs and verifies safety-related work.

questions.question: Why should a near miss be reported even though no injury occurred?
options: To replace all routine inspections
To prove that no hazard exists
To avoid discussing the event
To learn about causes before a similar event produces harm
questions.explanation: A near miss can reveal conditions also present in a damaging event. Reporting supports learning and prevention.

questions.question: Which response to near-miss reports best supports a learning culture?
options: Make the reporting process clear and encourage reports without automatic punishment
Publish personal accusations before investigation
Accept reports only after an injury
Treat every report as proof of incompetence
questions.explanation: People are more likely to report useful information when the process and treatment of those involved are clear and fair.

questions.question: An unexpected email asks you to open an attachment to restore account access. What is the safer first response?
options: Open it to see whether it is genuine
Forward it widely for opinions
Avoid the attachment and report the suspicious message through the approved channel
Reply with your password
questions.explanation: Unexpected attachments and urgent account requests can be phishing. Reporting allows the responsible team to assess the message.

questions.question: Why use a different strong password for each personal account?
options: It makes accounts share one recovery code
A password exposed on one service is less useful for entering your other accounts
It removes the need to protect your device
It guarantees that phishing cannot succeed
questions.explanation: Password reuse lets one disclosure threaten several accounts. Unique passwords limit that particular risk.

questions.question: What is a useful role of a trusted password manager?
options: Sending passwords to anyone who requests them
Turning every password into your date of birth
Removing every account’s login requirement
Generating and securely storing different strong passwords
questions.explanation: A password manager helps maintain strong, distinct passwords without relying on memory for every account. Use it in line with applicable device policies.

questions.question: What does multifactor authentication add to an account login?
options: Another type of verification in addition to the password
A second copy of the same password
Automatic permission for every login attempt
A guarantee that the account cannot be compromised
questions.explanation: MFA adds a separate verification factor. It reduces dependence on a password alone but is not a guarantee against every attack.

questions.question: Why are software security updates important for a personal device?
options: They make all backups unnecessary
They allow everyone to use the same password
They can fix weaknesses that attackers could exploit
They prove every downloaded app is safe
questions.explanation: Security updates address known weaknesses. On company or safety-critical systems, changes must follow the authorised maintenance process.

questions.question: Why can a cyber incident affecting shipboard operational technology be a safety concern?
options: OT only stores crew holiday photos
It can affect systems involved in physical ship operations
All OT is isolated from every possible input
Cyber incidents only change email formatting
questions.explanation: Operational technology can influence physical processes. Disruption can therefore have consequences beyond loss of office data.

questions.question: A personal USB drive contains a useful document. What should determine whether it can be connected to a ship’s system?
options: Whether the drive looks new
Whether the file name sounds official
Whether someone used it on another vessel
The company’s authorised removable-media controls
questions.explanation: Removable media can introduce unwanted software. The company’s controls, not appearance or convenience, govern its use.

questions.question: What is the main purpose of system backups in cyber resilience?
options: To support restoration of data and systems after disruption
To replace access controls
To make unsafe attachments harmless
To eliminate the need for incident planning
questions.explanation: Backups support recovery. They complement protection and response arrangements rather than replace them.

questions.question: A crew member notices a possible cyber incident on a company system. Which approach supports an organised response?
options: Experiment with unapproved repair tools
Conceal it unless another user complains
Use the established reporting and incident-response arrangements
Assume a restart is always authorised
questions.explanation: Reporting and response plans help the responsible personnel coordinate action. Unauthorised changes can interfere with that response.

questions.question: Can a well-intentioned person create a cyber risk without trying to cause harm?
options: No, only deliberate attackers create risk
Yes, careless actions or inappropriate changes can expose weaknesses
No, an antivirus icon rules out that possibility
Only if the person works ashore
questions.explanation: Cyber risk includes accidental actions as well as deliberate attacks. Awareness is relevant to all users.
